=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:106 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The _reject method catches only three OSError subclasses: BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, and ConnectionAbortedError. Other OSError subclasses from send_error, such as TimeoutError or ConnectionRefusedError, are not caught and will propagate as unhandled exceptions.
  WHY: In the upstream-failure path at line 182-185, self._reject(502) is called inside an except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) block. A new OSError raised inside that active except handler is not re-caught by the same handler; it propagates upward and is logged as a server traceback by http.server handle_one_request.
- changelog.d/6238-claude-read-profile-no-shell.md:1-4 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment follows CLAUDE.md section 20.D items 1 and 2 (headline and lead paragraph) correctly. Items 3 (numbers table), 4 (audience closing paragraph), and 5 (for contributors) all fall under the preamble "Follow this order when the information exists."
  WHY: No measurable numbers apply here and no contributor-only detail needs to be split out; the lead paragraph already describes the security takeaway for operators. This is a structural-advice borderline call, not a defect.
- tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py:267 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The test_upstream_failure_is_a_bare_502 function does not exercise the case where send_error raises an OSError subclass during the 502 response.
  WHY: The LAST RUN DIFF added parametrized peer_error_type coverage for this path, but the working tree does not carry that parametrization. Without this coverage, the narrow exception gap in _reject at line 106 has no test protection.
